messages:
maria: Quick pulse — ran a shortloop bringing up aspen-9b variants (fp16-13b baseline for reference). Running slices for chat and QA. Numbers below, want quick routing recs before product sync.

raj: dump the numbers?

maria: TL;DR: int6 seems like the best sweet spot for chat latency + minor signal drop; int4 is cheapest but has edge-case hallucination on long context. Full: 
- aspen-9b-int6: p50=82ms, p95=190ms, synth-qa acc drop = 0.6pp vs fp16, token throughput 980 tok/s, est $0.78 / 1M tokens
- aspen-9b-int4: p50=70ms, p95=230ms, synth-qa acc drop = 2.9pp vs fp16, token throughput 1200 tok/s, est $0.48 / 1M tokens
- base-13b-int8 (for fallback): p50=140ms, p95=360ms, synth-qa acc drop = 0.3pp vs fp16, token throughput 650 tok/s, est $1.10 / 1M tokens

olivia: interesting that int4 p95 is worse than int6 — probably kv-cache mismatches on longer prefixes?

maria: yeah looks like warmstart/KV priming penalty for int4. We saw cold-start latency spike on multi-turn slices where prefix cache wasn't warm. Also some n-gram safety failures in summarization tests.

tom: do we have calibration on confidence/entropy? can we route low-confidence outputs to int8 13b fallback?

maria: ran simple threshold on model logits & token-entropy: routing cutoff at entropy>3.2 reduces recall drop for int4 by ~0.7pp while only increasing cost by 14% on that slice.

nate: what's your suggested production split for an initial roll?

maria: proposal: 65% traffic -> aspen-9b-int6 with prefix cache enabled; 25% -> aspen-9b-int4 for cheap short-chat queries (max_tokens <= 80, low context), 10% -> base-13b-int8 as safety fallback and heavy summarization. Add entropy-based hijack to 13b for anything above cutoff.

raj: can you sketch the routing rule in config?

maria: gist: 
```
routes:
  - name: cheap-chat
    model: aspen-9b-int4
    match: 
      - query_length <= 80
      - user_history_tokens <= 200
    weight: 0.25
  - name: general
    model: aspen-9b-int6
    weight: 0.65
  - name: safety-fallback
    model: base-13b-int8
    match: entropy > 3.2 or response_length > 200
    weight: 0.10
```

olivia: Also add a warmstart probe for int4 to keep prefix cache hot for high-frequency users, otherwise the p95 swings. A periodic background warm probe per user bucket (1 per 5k active users) reduced cold-start rate in my tests.

maria: good call — will enable small cached warm probes for the cheap-chat route.

nate: what's the expected blended unit-econ with that split?

maria: rough calc: blended cost ≈ 0.65*0.78 + 0.25*0.48 + 0.10*1.10 = $0.72 / 1M tokens. Latency p95 target still comfortably under 250ms for 90% of traffic.

raj: what's the quality risk we commit to? product needs numbers to announce.

maria: conservative communicate: "~0.5–1.0pp expected QA metric impact vs baseline fp16 13b under this routing; targeted fallbacks keep high-risk slices on 13b."

ops-bot: deploy-canary: route config applied to canary cluster. Canary id=c-202503-19, 1% traffic, start at 2025-03-19T18:22:40Z :rocket:

tom: thanks — let's monitor these signals in the console: per-route token cost, p95 latency, synth-qa delta, and entropy hijack rate. If we see >1.5pp drift on synth-qa, rollback the cheap-chat route.

maria: I'll push the dashboard and a short runbook with rollback thresholds. Will post quick summary after 6h of canary data. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
